These endpoints enable to access order-item data. ## Filtering Options The endpoint supports filtering by: | Parameter | Type | Description | |-----------|------|-------------| | `order_ids` | array[integer] | List of specific order IDs | | `plan_ids` | array[integer] | List of specific plan (event) IDs | | `date_field` | string | Date field to filter on (`CREATED_DATE_UTC`, `UPDATED_DATE_UTC`, or `EVENT_START_DATE_UTC`). `UPDATED_DATE_UTC` filters on when the order **data** last changed (any field of the flattened record, including nested/enrichment fields such as plan name), matching the `updated_date_utc` field in the response — not the order's own update time (`order_updated_date_utc`). | | `date_from` | string | Start date for the selected date field. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm` or `YYYY-MM-DD` | | `date_to` | string | End date for the selected date field. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm` or `YYYY-MM-DD` | ## Model documentation #### Orders with Order Items The goal of this endpoint is to provide a comprehensive picture about orders with detailed information about their associated order items, including buyers, owners, partners, plans, sessions, and more.
📄 /reports/order-items response entity model | Column Name | Description | Example value | |----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------| | `id` | Unique order ID. This code groups all tickets bought in the same transaction. | 12345 | | `parent_order_id` | If the order comes from a reschedule, the original order ID | 11234 | | `buyer` | Order buyer information. | _See `order.buyer` documentation below_ | | `created_date_utc` | UTC date when the order was created. | 2021-01-01T00:00:00Z | | `updated_date_utc` | UTC date when the order **data** was last updated — moves whenever any field of the flattened order record changes (including nested/enrichment fields such as plan name, UTM or ratings). This is the field the `UPDATED_DATE_UTC` filter matches, so filtering by `UPDATED_DATE_UTC` and this value are always consistent. | 2021-01-01T00:00:00Z | | `order_updated_date_utc` | UTC date when the order **itself** was last updated (order-level fields only). Unlike `updated_date_utc`, it does not move when only nested/enrichment data changes. | 2021-01-01T00:00:00Z | | `surcharge` | Surcharge applied to the order. | 0.0 | | `currency` | ISO3 currency of the order monetary fields. | USD | | `purchase_channel` | Purchase channel where the transaction comes from. | web | | `channel` | Channel slug through which this order was placed. Use this field to join with `POST /v1/reports/channels/search` — the `channel` field in both endpoints is the same slug. `null` when no channel is recorded on the order (e.g. box-office or pre-channel data). | partner-channel | | `payment_method` | Payment method used. | credit_card | | `purchase_location_source` | Purchase location information. | _See `order.purchase_location_source` documentation below_ | | `billing_zip_code` | Billing ZIP Code manually fulfilled by the customer. | 28001 | | `utm` | UTM information attributed to the order. | _See `order.utm` documentation below_ | | `partner` | Partner information. | _See `order.partner` documentation below_ | | `business` | Business associated with the order. | _See `order.business` documentation below_ | | `plan` | Plan information. | _See `order.plan` documentation below_ | | `coupon` | Coupon information. | _See `order.coupon` documentation below_ | | `assigned_seats` | List of assigned seats for the order. | _See `order.assigned_seats` documentation below_ | | `order_items` | List of order items associated with this order. | _See `order.order_items` documentation below_ | | `booking_questions` | List of booking questions and answers for the order. | _See `order.booking_questions` documentation below_ | | `order_group_id` | 🚧 **Under Development.** Groups orders from cluster tickets. All orders with the same `order_group_id` belong to the same purchase group (e.g., bundled tickets across multiple venues). | 12345 | | `is_main_group_order` | 🚧 **Under Development.** Flag indicating whether this is the main order in a group. `true` for the primary order, `false` for secondary orders in the same group. | true | | `staff_notes` | List of staff notes attached to the order. Opt-in: only returned when the search request includes `included_fields=staff_notes`; otherwise the field is omitted from the response. | `["Payment Details: Groupon", "change ticket to new day"]` | | `booked_slots` | List of booked slots (assets/rooms reserved by the cart). | _See `order.booked_slots` documentation below_ | | `payment_details` | Card payment details for the order (transaction id, brand and descriptive payment method). Empty/null when the order was not paid by card or no card details are recorded. | _See `order.payment_details` documentation below_ |

description.content:
Access detailed event sales data through a reliable REST API. # Introduction The Fever Reporting API is a RESTful service that gives our partners access to in-depth insights into their event sales on Fever. With this API, partners can retrieve comprehensive order data, including ticket information, financial details (revenue, surcharges, discounts), plan details, and basic customer data. ## Primary Use Cases This API is intended for partners who want to integrate Fever sales data into their internal systems—such as CRMs, Business Intelligence (BI) platforms, data warehouses, or ERP systems. ## What It’s Not For **This API is not designed for real-time operational use cases like access control or live inventory tracking.** For those needs, please refer to other Fever APIs specifically built for operational workflows. ## Getting Access Access to the Fever Reporting API is granted individually. To request access, reach out to your Fever sales representative. They’ll walk you through the process. Once approved, you'll receive credentials to authenticate and begin using the API. ## Extended Documentation (for Authorized Partners) Once your access is approved and credentials are issued, you’ll be able to view the full technical documentation here: [🔒 Extended Documentation](https://data-reporting-api.prod.feverup.com/v1/documentation). If you haven’t received your credentials yet, you can still access the public section of our documentation, which covers most of the key technical information. ## Playground (for Authorized Partners) After receiving your API credentials, you can access the [▶️ Fever - Reporting API Playground](https://data-reporting-api.prod.feverup.com/v1/playground) to explore and test available endpoints. The Playground is a Swagger UI interface that allows you to: - Browse detailed documentation for each endpoint - Execute live API requests directly from your browser - Authentication is required, so be sure to log in with your credentials before using the interface. ## Status Page We are committed to providing a reliable service for our users. To ensure transparency, you can subscribe to our [📣 Status Page](https://status.data-reporting-api.prod.feverup.com/) to stay informed about: - Scheduled maintenance that may temporarily affect the availability of the Reporting API - Ongoing incidents and issues impacting the performance or functionality of the API - Resolutions and updates on incidents in real-time By subscribing, you will receive timely notifications via email, Slack, etc., keeping you updated on any events that might impact your integration with the Reporting API.

# Quickstart ### Code samples
🐍 Python code sample to extract data from /example-endpoint endpoint ```python import json import time from typing import Any import requests class RAPIConnector: def __init__(self, hostname: str, username: str, password: str) -> None: self.hostname = hostname self.__username = username self.__password = password self.__access_token = self.__get_access_token() def __get_access_token(self) -> str: response = requests.post( f"https://{self.hostname}/v1/auth/token", data={"username": self.__username, "password": self.__password} ) response.raise_for_status() return response.json()["access_token"] def __get_request_headers(self) -> dict[str, str]: return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.__access_token}"} def post_example_endpoint(self, search_params: dict[str, Any]) -> requests.Response: response = requests.post( f"https://{self.hostname}/v1/example-endpoint/search", headers=self.__get_request_headers(), json=search_params, ) response.raise_for_status() return response def get_example_endpoint( self, search_id: str, page: int = 0) -> requests.Response: return requests.get( f"https://{self.hostname}/v1/example-endpoint/search/{search_id}", headers=self.__get_request_headers(), params={"page": page}, ) def fetch_all_order_items(self, search_params: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]: search = self.post_example_endpoint(search_params=search_params) search_id = search.json()["search_id"] is_ready = False n_attempts = 0 while not is_ready and n_attempts < 10: search = self.get_example_endpoint(search_id=search_id) is_ready = True if search.status_code == 200 else False if not is_ready: print(f"{search.status_code} - Waiting search result to be ready...") n_attempts += 1 time.sleep(1) if n_attempts == 10: raise Exception("Search result is not ready after 10 attempts") # Fetch all pages data = search.json()["data"] partition_info = search.json()["partition_info"] total_rows = 0 print(f"Found a total of {len(partition_info)} partitions") for partition in partition_info: page = partition["partition_num"] total_rows += int(partition["rows"]) if page == 0: continue print(f"Fetching partition {page}...") search = self.get_example_endpoint(search_id=search_id, page=page) data += search.json()["data"] assert len(data) == total_rows return data def main() -> None: hostname = "data-reporting-api.prod.feverup.com" username = "" password = "" rapi_connector = RAPIConnector(hostname=hostname, username=username, password=password) search_params = { "date_field": "CREATED_DATE_UTC", "date_from": "2024-01-01", "date_to": "2024-02-01", } raw_path = "example_endpoint_raw.json" print("### Extracting data from Reporting API ###") data = rapi_connector.fetch_all_order_items(search_params=search_params) # Save the raw data to a JSON file with open(raw_path, "w") as f: f.write(json.dumps(data, indent=4)) print(f"Data extracted and saved to {raw_path}") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
## Authentication The first step is to authenticate with the API. The API uses the OAuth 2.0 protocol to authenticate users. In order to fetch a valid token, you must use the following endpoint: - `POST /oauth/token` -> It will return a valid `token` to be used in the following requests from your `username` and `password` credentials.
➡️ Example curl request ```shell curl -X 'POST' 'https://data-reporting-api.prod.feverup.com/v1/auth/token' -H 'Accept: application/json' -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d 'username=&password=' ``` Remember to replace `` and `` with the correct values.
➡️ Example response ```json { "access_token": "", "token_type": "bearer" } ```
## How to request data for any endpoint in the Reporting API? The approach is analogous for all the endpoints in the API. The API works with asynchronous requests that return paginated results. This means that for every request, you will need to follow these steps: 1. Create a request asynchronously, in order to obtain a **search ID**. When creating this request, certain parameters might be requested in order to filter the expected data, like entity IDs, dates, etc. 2. Fetch the paginated results for the requested data. This step will require the **search ID** obtained in the previous step, and it will return the paginated data for the requested report.
➡️ Example requesting data for /reports/order-items endpoint ### 1. Create the request asynchronously to get order items data The first step is to create a new search asynchronously in order to fetch the order items. You can do this by sending a `POST` request to the endpoint. - `POST /xxx/search`: It will create a new search. The request body must contain the search criteria, allowing to search by creation or update date among other parameters, depending on the endpoint itself. The response will contain the * *search ID** that you can later use to fetch the paginated result.
➡️ Example curl request ```shell curl -X 'POST' 'https://data-reporting-api.prod.feverup.com/v1/xxx/search' -H 'accept: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "param_a": "" }' ``` Remember to replace `` with the correct value. You can check all the accepted parameters in the endpoints documentation (available in private docs).
➡️ Example response ```json { "message": "Asynchronous execution in progress. Use provided query id to perform query monitoring and management.", "search_id": "" } ``` The response will contain the **search ID** that you can use to fetch the paginated result afterwards.
### 2. Fetch the paginated results for the requested data The last step is to fetch the search result data. You can do this by sending a `GET` request to the `/xxx/{search_id}` endpoint. - `GET /xxx/?page=`: It will return the search data for the given ID and page number. By default, the page number is `0`, and only mandatory columns are returned.
➡️ Example curl request ```shell curl -X 'GET' 'https://data-reporting-api.prod.feverup.com/v1/xxx/search/ -H 'accept: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ' ``` For instance, this request will retrieve all mandatory fields plus `aaa` and `bbb` fields. Remember to replace ``, and `` with the correct values. Once the output is ready to be consumed, it will return a JSON object containing the orders data for the given search ID and page number. Otherwise, it will return a `202` status code with a message indicating that the data is still being processed.
➡️ Example response ```json { "partition_info": [ { "partition_num": 0, "endpoint": "/?page=0", "size": 1234, "rows": 100 }, { "partition_num": 1, "endpoint": "/?page=1", "size": 5678, "rows": 100 } ], "data": [ "your data records" ] } ```


# Rate limits The Fever Reporting API has rate limits on its endpoints. - **Authentication**: 20 requests/minute. - **Other endpoints**: 200 requests/minute. If you exceed these limits, you will receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response. In this case, you should wait for one minute before making additional requests.

# FAQ >
> 💬 How are cancellations handled in the API? >
> > In the `/reports/order-items` endpoint, cancellations are handled at the individual order item level. Each order item represents a single unit (ticket, add-on, etc.) within an order. > > When an order item is canceled, its `status` field will change to `CANCELED`. > >
> 💡 Example > > #### Before cancellation > ```json lines > { > "id": 12345, // order id > ... > "order_items": [ > { > "id": 1910920, > "status": "PURCHASED", > "barcode": "ABC123", > "owner": { > "name": "Alice" > } > ... > }, > { > "id": 1910921, > "status": "PURCHASED", > "barcode": "DEF456", > "owner": { > "name": "Bob" > } > ... > } > ] > } > ``` > > #### After cancellation of one order item > ```json lines > { > "id": 12345, // order id > ... > "order_items": [ > { > "id": 1910920, > "status": "CANCELED", > "barcode": "ABC123", > "owner": { > "name": "Alice" > } > ... > }, > { > "id": 1910921, > "status": "PURCHASED", > "barcode": "DEF456", > "owner": { > "name": "Bob" > } > ... > } > ] > } > ``` >
>

>
> 💬 How are transfers handled in the API? >
> > In the `/reports/order-items` endpoint, transfers are handled at the individual order item level. Each order item represents a single unit, so when an order item is transferred, the owner information is updated to reflect the new owner. > > When an order item is transferred, the `owner` field will be updated with the new owner's information. The order item maintains its `PURCHASED` status but now belongs to the new owner. > >
> 💡 Example > > #### Before transfer > ```json lines > { > "id": 12345, // order id > // ... order fields > "order_items": [ > { > "id": 1910920, > "status": "PURCHASED", > "barcode": "ABC123", > "owner": { > "name": "Alice", > "email": "alice@example.com" > } > ... > }, > { > "id": 1910921, > "status": "PURCHASED", > "barcode": "DEF456", > "owner": { > "name": "Bob", > "email": "bob@example.com" > } > ... > } > ] > } > ``` > > #### After transfer of one order item > ```json lines > { > "id": 12345, // order id > ... > "order_items": [ > { > "id": 1910920, > "status": "PURCHASED", > "barcode": "ABC123", > "owner": { > "name": "Charlie", > "email": "charlie@example.com" > } > ... > }, > { > "id": 1910921, > "status": "PURCHASED", > "barcode": "DEF456", > "owner": { > "name": "Bob", > "email": "bob@example.com" > } > ... > } > ] > } > ``` >
>

>
> 💬 How is the param UPDATED_DATE_UTC updated in the `/reports/order-items` endpoint? >
> Please note that not all fields in the returned JSON are eligible to update the value of UPDATED_DATE_UTC. Only fields directly related to the purchase and order items themselves will trigger a change in this value. >
